China's 15-FYP Carbon Peaking Action Plan; CGN and YZP 2Q power generation update

China's latest decarbonization policy package—anchored by the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) Carbon Peaking Action Plan and followed by the NEA's 2026–2028 energy-saving and carbon-reduction plan—sets clearer targets and execution measures to expand non-fossil energy, strengthen grid flexibility, curb reliance on coal/oil, and accelerate economy-wide efficiency and electrification, which we see as supportive for grid/renewables equipment makers and renewable operators. Against this backdrop, CGN Power delivered 2Q26 nuclear generation of 58,640 GWh (+3.5% YoY), and we maintain OW as a potentially improving 2026/27 tariff regime could drive earnings growth. Yangtze Power (YZP) reported 2Q26 hydropower generation of 70.9bn kWh (+2.8% YoY), and remains our preferred defensive name amid China's easing rate cycle.

- China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) Carbon Peaking Action Plan (9 Jul 2026) sets 2030 targets of a 17% cut in CO\( _{2} \) intensity vs. 2025 and 25% non-fossil energy, calling for faster buildout of renewables/nuclear, more grid flexibility (UHV, storage, demand response), reduced coal/oil reliance, and broad industrial, building and transport decarbonization supported by tighter standards and expanded carbon/green-certificate markets. Shortly after, the NEA's 2026–2028 energy-saving and carbon-reduction plan (10 Jul 2026) adds near-term execution: lift non-fossil share by ~1ppt per year to 2028, raise efficient coal capacity by ~15ppt, pilot low/zero-carbon mines/oilfields/parks, and push coal plant upgrades/retirements, CCUS/co-firing pilots, renewables integration, cleaner upstream operations, and demand-side electrification. We see the potential to benefit grid/renewable power equipment manufacturers and renewable power operators. For renewable equipment makers, we prefer Orient Cables, GW-H, Deye and Sungrow. For power equipment manufacturers, we like TGOOD Electric and their recent management call reinforces our positive view on their new orders from data centers, overseas utilities and their break-through to AIDC products. We also like Wasion.

- For renewable power operators, CGN Power's 2Q26 update reported nuclear generation of 58,640 GWh (+3.5% YoY), driven by higher output at Daya Bay, Lingdong and Ningde plus the start of commercial operations at Huizhou and Cangnan, partly offset by weaker Taishan generation. We maintain our OW rating, as a potentially improving tariff regime in 2026/27 could drive earnings growth. Yangtze Power's 2Q26 update reported hydropower generation of 70.9bn kWh (+2.8% YoY), driven by stronger output at Three Gorges and Gezhouba stations, partly offset by weaker generation at Xiluodu, Xiangjiaba, Wudongde, and Baihetan. We favor Yangtze Power as a defensive pick amid China's easing rate cycle.

China announced the 15-FYP Carbon Peaking Action Plan

China announced the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) Carbon Peaking Action Plan on July 9, 2026. The plan views the 15-FYP as decisive for reaching peak emissions on schedule. It targets by 2030 a 17% drop in  \( CO_{2} \)  emissions per unit of GDP versus 2025 and a 25% share of non-fossil energy, while steadily peaking coal and oil consumption and embedding green, low-carbon requirements across the economy. Key measures include rapid expansion of wind/solar/hydro/nuclear and stronger grid flexibility (UHV transmission, storage, pumped hydro, demand response), cleaner substitution away from coal and improved oil/gas use with more green fuels (hydrogen/ammonia/methanol, biofuels/SAF). It also mandates industrial upgrading and efficiency retrofits, builds zero-carbon parks/factories and greener data centers, promotes circular economy actions, and accelerates low-carbon buildings and transport (including higher EV adoption), backed by tighter laws/standards, better emissions accounting, finance and pricing reforms, and expanded carbon and green-certificate markets with clearer local accountability.

Shortly after this announcement, the National Energy Administration (NEA) announced the Energy Sector Energy-Saving and Carbon-Reduction Action Plan (2026–2028) on July 10, 2026. The plan sets a three-year push to cut energy use and emissions across the entire energy chain—production through end-use—while accelerating the shift from fossil fuels to non-fossil energy. By 2028, it aims to raise the non-fossil share by about 1 percentage point per year, increase by roughly 15 percentage points the share of coal power capacity meeting benchmark efficiency standards, and build pilot low/zero-carbon mines, oilfields, and industrial parks. Key actions include retiring or upgrading coal plants, piloting co-firing and CCUS, expanding transmission and storage to absorb more renewables, and reducing emissions in coal and oil & gas operations through electrification, efficiency upgrades, and circular resource use. On the demand side, it promotes renewable-powered industrial parks and microgrids, greener transport and charging infrastructure, cleaner buildings/rural energy, and low-carbon heating—backed by stronger R&D, digital carbon management, improved emissions accounting, and expanded green power/certificate market mechanisms.

JPM view: We view most of the policy targets as largely a continuation of previous policy objectives, and most of them align with our expectations. Within the renewables space, we have OW ratings on Goldwind-H (2208 HK), Orient Cables (603606 CH), Sungrow (300274 CH), Deye (605117 CH), Arctech (688408 CH), GCL Tech (3800 HK), Daqo (DQ US), CGN Power (1816 HK), and Yangtze Power (600900 CH). We like power equipment makers like Wasion Holdings (3393HK) and TGOOD Electric (300001.CH).
CGN Power announced its 2Q operation update

CGN Power announced its 2Q operation update on July 10, 2026. Its 2Q26 nuclear power generation was 58,640GWh, up \(3.5\%\) yoy. This was mainly driven by a rise in nuclear power generation at Daya Bay units, Lingdong units, and Ningde units, and the start of commercial operation of Huizhou and Cangnan units, while partly offset by a decline in Taishan units.

JPM view: Capacity addition is positive for CGN Power's power generation growth. We see a potentially improving tariff regime for CGN Power in 2026/27, which may lead to earnings growth. Thus, we have an OW rating on CGN Power.

Yangtze Power announced its 2Q power generation

Yangtze Power announced its 2Q power generation data on July \(6^{\text{th}}\), 2026. Its 2Q26 hydropower generation was 70.9bn kWh, up \(2.8\%\) yoy. This was mainly driven by a rise in power generation at Three Gorges and Gezhouba hydropower stations, while partly offset by Xiluodu, Xiangjiaba, Wudongde, and Baihetan hydropower stations.

JPM view: For investors seeking defensive names, Yangtze Power is our preferred pick, on the back of China's easing rate cycle. Our positive stance on the name rests on: 1) its business model being the most defensive among China IPPs; and 2) its low gearing, strong cash flow and dividend commitment.
Qingdao TGOOD Electric - Key takeaways from the management call

Qingdao TGOOD Electric has outperformed the index by \(\sim 20\%\) YTD (TGOOD \(+21\%\) vs. SZCOMP \(+1.5\%\)) as investors increasingly recognize its rising overseas exposure in prefabricated substations and the growth potential of its data-center offering. The recent management call reinforces our positive view: China data-center orders YTD have already exceeded the FY25 level and management has guided to a doubling of China DC orders this year; Middle East prefabricated substation orders could more than double this year with management guiding to \(\sim 50\%\) market share, alongside rising orders from Europe and Australia; and the collaboration with Eaton (ETN US, NR) could help TGOOD expand further overseas, while its newly developed high-voltage AC-to-low-voltage DC solutions have attracted inquiries from data-center customers across regions, including the US. At \(< 20x\) 1-year forward P/E, we think the valuation remains attractive, and we reiterate our OW rating (note).
